title: Deck Maker run
description: One deck run. `deck` is engine/deck/deck.schema.json's deck.json as the engine writes it; the rest is what the screens need around it.

inputs.description: What a deck is built from (ADR 0023, amended by 0028): the person's prompt text, documents they attach, and the brief and research read from data.upstream. The brief and research are derived, never stored here.

text.description: The open prompt, of any length. Its n-th sentence is cited as prompt:<n>.

format.description: How the deck will be used: pitch (presented on a screen) or full ('Sent to be read', the leave-behind: every slide in story order, detailed). Written by the format switch under the type picker.

deck_type.description: deck-types: the person's explicit pick on the type picker, the first step of Start. It ranks above an answer to q_deck_type, an inference from the brief and the default (run_deck --type). Absent or null ('Not sure: decide from my brief'): no pick, so the answer, then a high-confidence inference, then agency_pitch decide. Kept in inputs, not in deck (deck is the engine's own output and is replaced on every build).

by.description: Who picked: the person (the app writes 'person'), or human:<id> when known.

confirmed_stages.description: The person's yes on the Change sheet to the new writing a type change needs (the model stages it runs). Without it a change that needs a stage not yet recorded is refused (409 needs_stages) before anything runs or spends.

library.description: Presented look and pictures (ADR 0027, accepted 2026-11-17): the gate for the picture, Style Pack and brand preferences. Off or absent: they are not shown, the runner ignores them, and the deck is today's.

documents.description: The files the person attached (display list).

pictures.description: Not appearance: generating can spend money and send a prompt out. Ordinary attributed decisions, written by the app.

source.description: Where may the pictures come from? existing: only pictures we already have (territory frames and uploads); generated: also make new ones, up to cap_usd for this deck (the amount can be changed). existing never calls a provider: nothing is sent out and nothing is spent.

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

approval.description: Who approves pictures before a client sees them? owner: me, the deck's owner; named: someone else (user). What should a picture be labelled until it is approved? Illustrative (up to 30 characters, no digit, so it never reads as a figure). A frame approved in the Territory tool is not approved here: it arrives made.

user.description: With approver: named, the approver as human:<id>.

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

text_mode.description: condense: the repair loop may shorten a slide's text to fit; preserve: it never does. Written by the app.

production.description: The Production file this deck's pictures come from (deck-prod-picker): a .clan or export zip the person attached, which the engine holds by its sha256 (attach_production) and reads on every build (--production). fetch and look are the person's opt-ins: fetching picked https pictures (still limited to the engine's host allow-list) and the vision check that only flags. Written by the app.

items.description: The content box of a running stage: what it is reading or writing, one row each.

gate.description: The open gate. Nothing past it runs until a person approves.

agent.description: The circle at the gate; Strategy for gates 1 and 2, Idea for gate 3 when absent.

territories.description: Gate 2: the territories to pick from.

first_pick.description: Gate 2: the id of the blind judge's first pick.

picked.description: Gate 2: the id the person picked.

idea.description: Gate 3: the one idea and the work that carries it.

territory_name.description: The picked territory's name, for the line under the gate's title when run.gate.territories is not carried.

approvals.description: gate id (or `deck`) -> who approved and when; a gate approval may also say what was decided.

deck.description: The deck approval at Review (Approve the deck): who, when, and the decision. Written by the app until the server writes it.

agent.description: What the agent circle shows: which agent, doing what, which step of how many. Optional; written by the server, or by a fixture until then. `slow` is a flag, never a time.

to.description: Hand-off: the agent the work passes to.

error.description: With state failed: which stage failed and whether it can be retried.

done.description: With state done: what is ready.

checks.description: While no gate is open: what has been checked so far in this run, shown as Checked so far. Optional; written by the server, or by a fixture until then.

decisions.description: Every approve, edit or retry at a gate, in order, and the deck approval (gate `deck`).

gate_requests.description: An edit or retry asked for at a gate, recorded like change_requests; launches nothing.

types.description: deck-types, written by the engine: which deck types it offers. recipes: whether DECK_RECIPES (with DECK_LOOK_V3) is on; offered: the type ids the picker may show (a type that joined with the recipes is hidden while they are off).

deck.description: deck.json: meta, order, slides keyed by id, requirements. Plus appendix_count.

type.description: The deck type the deck was built for.

confirm.description: What a person should confirm: every proposal, every figure only their own statement or a low-confidence pin supports, every slide still needing a person (engine intake.confirm_list).

confirm_summary.description: total, verified, supplied, sourced, open, needs_person (engine intake.confirm_summary).

theme.description: The look the deck used (theme.Theme made visible), written by the runner.

from.description: Which tier gave each token: a colour role, head, body or logo. Written by the runner (deck-look-kits). meta.theme.source is the highest tier that gave any token.

style_pack.description: The Style Pack the deck's look and pictures used: its document, version and computed style hash (deck-look-kits).

agency.description: The agency look the deck wore: its id and revision, so Review can say the look changed since the last build (deck-look-kits).

accent_line.description: The accent where it is a thin line, rule or chart series. Set when the accent is under 3:1 on the paper (a pale accent is a fill only); absent means the accent itself.

held.description: What the look held back and why (for example a client logo whose brand is not the brief's client). Never dropped silently.

repair_policy.description: How the repair loop runs (engine/deck/policy/repair.yaml; a profile may override). The policy a run used is stamped at deck.meta.repair_policy by the runner.

severity.description: Check name to severity. Every key is a check name of spec.ISSUE_CHECKS.

word_rule.description: delete_only (default): the new text is an ordered subsequence of the same field's base words and only allow-listed words (assemble.DELETABLE, or `deletable`) are deleted; reuse: content words of the base text in any order, refused on a client deck.

deletable.description: Replaces the default allow-list of words that may be deleted (absent: assemble.DELETABLE). Fail closed: every other word survives.

enabled.description: The vision critic stays advisory and off until its questions are graded.

preferences.description: The resolved preferences a build used, each the field's values plus source: person or default. Written by the runner.

hash.description: The 8-hex hash of the Style Pack the deck now uses (the runner's stamp); a picture whose style hash differs is stale, not mixed.

hold.description: True when the Style Pack could not be read (a StyleError): the build went on and the pictures keep the style they were made in.

look.description: deck-graphics: the switchable parts a person turned on or off for this deck (read only under DECK_GRAPHICS=1): icons, mockups.

size.description: deck-slide-size: the slide size the deck is drawn at (theme.CANVASES), written only when a person, the document or a recipe gave one; absent means 16:9.

style_hold.description: Set when a Style Pack was given but could not be used (it broke its rules or could not be read). The deck was built with the default style and pictures are held: image steps (deck-frames-in, deck-image-gen) read this and make nothing until a person fixes the pack.

production.description: The Production Tool export this deck's pulled pictures were taken from (deck-prod-assets), the shape of Production's own briefs[].source. offer_sha256 (the offered entity ids and asset hashes) is the update key, never the relay ETag. Optional: a deck with no pulled picture has none.

how.description: bundle: the export zip through deck.from_production; clan: a Production .clan (or the zip) read by deck.prod_picker, which picks from metadata and pulls only the picked pictures; os: from the OS (later).

appendix_count.description: How many appendix slides; the fallback when appendix_ids is absent.

appendix_ids.description: Slide ids kept in the appendix.

supplied.description: A human-only slide the engine rebuilt from what the person supplied (engine assemble._fill_human_only): basis, by, refs.

layout.description: Which layout the slide is drawn with and why. Written by the layout plan (code); a person's swap is look.layouts.<slide id>, stamped here. Absent: the renderer works it out as today.

id.description: A library layout id, or flow (reserved: no library layout, no slots).

moved.description: Points the layout plan moved to the speaker notes: an overlay, never an edit of the blocks. block is the index in slide.blocks, item the index in its items (null: the whole block), sha the first 12 hex of the verbatim text, refs the point's refs.

cpl.description: Characters per line the slide was fitted at when 48 would not fit (60): the last step before type goes to the caption floor.

title_pt.description: deck-slide-size: the title size this one slide was fitted at at 4:3 or A4 when the layout's stamped size would not fit (the last rung before no_fit).

blocks_sha.description: First 12 hex of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of [title, shown blocks] when the slots were bound. A different hash makes layout and slots read as absent.

slots.description: Blocks bound to the layout's named boxes, keyed by slot name so each is a data path (deck.slides.s07.slots.picture). Written by code, never by the app. The blocks stay the only source of words.

blocks.description: Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.
Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.
Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.
Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.
Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.
Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.

image.description: The request for one picture and the person's decision on it. What was made is on deck.assets. Written by the image plan and image step; approval is the runner's stamp of review.images.

key.description: The frame key <territory id>-<shot>-<flash|pro>, a material id, or a Brand Clan logo id, or a Production Tool item key (an entity id; a key visual is <format set id>#master).

run.description: The territory run's 12-character hash, or for a Production picture the first 12 hex of the exported .clan's sha256.

subject.description: What a camera could see, from the slide's own creative text. No brand name, person's name, figure or words to paint.

prompt.description: The exact text sent: subject, style block, guard rails. Recorded, never edited by hand.

basis.description: Every picture is creative, never sourced. There is no stored label: a renderer draws the picture label when status is not approved.

alt.description: Written by code from subject. Never from a picture's metadata.

reason.description: Why the slot is empty, failed or held back.

approval.description: The runner's stamp of review.images.<slide id>.<slot>. An approval names one asset: a changed asset is unapproved again. That approval.asset equals the slot's asset is checked in code, not by the schema.

candidate.description: A hero (pro) picture beside the approved draft (deck-image-gen). slot.asset stays the draft; only a person's approval of the candidate's own asset promotes it. Never drawn while pending, flagged or removed.

text_zone.description: deck-look (LOOK_V3): where words may sit on this picture, from images.text_zone (the calm-zone finder and scrim solver) or pinned by a repair or a person. A zone: the words' colour, the scrim's colour and alpha (0.40 to 0.60), the 10th-percentile contrast it predicts and the zone's luminance s.d. none: no zone reads at AA, so the words sit beside the picture.

blocks.description: Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.
Indexes, among the slide's shown blocks, this value was bound from.

pinned.description: The runner's stamp of review.pinned.<slide id>: the trim, the red team's reorder and the repair loop leave the slide's words and place alone.

assets.description: Pictures, keyed by img_ plus the first 12 hex of the file's SHA-256, so one file is one asset in every slot and run. Written by the image plan and image step.

file.description: assets/<sha256>.<ext> in the run folder; human/assets/ in the document.

rights.description: A reference_only asset is a style reference and never fills a slot. Client-supplied or unclear images default to reference_only.

source.description: Where a pulled picture came from (deck-prod-assets): the Production Tool project, the entity and its version, the asset's origin, the job that made it and the hash of the exported .clan. Never a file path or a URL.

evidence.description: ref -> { kind, text }: what each cited ref says, for the Evidence tab.

upstream.description: Frozen sources keyed by source document id (a brief, a research). Written by the host's spin-off; read-only for the app.

intake.description: The a0 intake as the runner writes it, plus the person's answers (written by the app).

origin.description: Where the option came from. The inferred deck type is 'proposed'.

source.description: The words in the person's own material the option rests on: a quote string, or { quote }.

kind.description: 'supply' is a card for something only the person knows (team, credentials, budget split, options, decision date). Free text, one item per line, skippable. Its answer fills the slide named by `fills`. 'preference' is a card for how the deck should look or what it may spend (docs/contracts/deck-visuals.md 6.4): the default option first, skippable; its answer also writes the addressed field. 'preference' is a card for how the deck should look or what it may spend (docs/contracts/deck-visuals.md 6.4): the default option first, skippable; its answer also writes the addressed field.

fills.description: A supply card: the human-only slide type its answer fills.

answers.description: qid -> the person's answer or skip.

verified.description: confirm ref -> the person's verify decision, written by the app (a human write). Only verified or supplied items count as sourced.

research_request.description: A request to strengthen with research. Recorded only: launching needs the server feature.

exports.description: What has been written, per format. Absent means 'Not built yet'. `true` and a file-name string are the older shapes; the object names the file.

change_requests.description: An Ask-for-a-change click. Words only; sources stay.

look.description: How the deck looks. It never changes what the deck says. A person's change here is one rolling 'look' entry and asks for no reason (os-layer 4). Written by the app: an intake answer, the Start screen or Review.

pictures.description: Which slides should carry pictures? creative_cover: the cover, section breaks and the creative slides (each territory, the idea, each execution, the audience); creative: the creative slides only; none: none; custom: I'll choose slide by slide. Evidence slides never get one. Default until Laurence answers; his answer replaces it: creative_cover.

slides.description: With on: custom, slide id to true or false; set at Review, only for a slide type that may carry a picture.

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

density.description: How much text should each slide carry? lean: about 30 words, the rest in the speaker notes; standard: up to about 60 words; detailed: the full text on the slide. Default: lean for a presented pitch (inputs.format pitch), detailed for a leave-behind (inputs.format full).

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

size.description: Which slide size? 16:9 (widescreen), 4:3 (standard) or a4 (A4 landscape, 297 x 210 mm). Absent: the recipe's default (presented: 16:9; sent to be read: a4; a tender response: a4). The engine's server forwards canvas as --size.

by.description: Who chose it: person (the Start screen) or human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

brand.description: Whose brand should the deck wear? agency: ours, with the client's logo on the cover; client: the client's; co_branded: both, side by side on the cover. A logo is placed only for a brand the information already names.

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

agency_look.description: Should the deck wear the agency's look? true (the default): an agency that has set up a look gets it on every new deck, with no switch to find; false: this deck opts out and uses the default theme. An agency with no look set up changes nothing (deck-look-kits, Sai, 17 Nov 2026).

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

update_requested.description: When the person chose 'update to current look' (ISO 8601). The runner takes the agency's current look at the next build, then the deck keeps that look again. Existing decks keep the look they were built with until then.

style_pack.description: Which Style Pack should the pictures follow? territory: the one the territory board uses; other: another one (document_id names it). Default until Laurence answers: the territory board and the deck share one Style Pack.

by.description: Who chose it, as human:<id>. Absent: nobody chose, the default is in force.

via.description: Where the choice was made: an intake question, the Start screen or Review.

strict_brand.description: Only the kit's layouts and given tokens; nothing derived.

layouts.description: Slide id to the layout a person swapped to. The runner stamps it as slide.layout with chosen_by person.

review.description: A person's review decisions, outside deck because the runner writes deck whole on every build. The runner stamps them onto the slides (pinned, image approval). Written by the app.

production.description: A person's swaps in the Production picker (deck-prod-picker P6): for a slide's slot, the candidate key they chose instead of the rule's pick. The engine honours one only while the key is still a candidate for that slot, and records it in its stages (production_choices.json). Written by the app.

qa.description: The checks' findings as issues, written by the runner beside validation and report. current is false once the deck has changed since deck_sha.

additionalProperties.description: One finding code can act on, from any source. Derived by adapters from validation.json, qa.json, slot checks and guard results; written by the runner.

id.description: First 8 hex of the SHA-256 of source|check|slide|slot|n, n counting repeats on one slide.

level.description: The source's own level, kept as written.

repair.description: The repair rounds, written by the runner. At most two.

production.description: What the Production picker did on the last build (deck-prod-picker; engine-owned, run_state.production_payload): the card line, each picked slot with its candidates (label, reach, rights, status; never a location), and the opt-in switches. Absent when the build used no Production file.
